record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Under what conditions on the stress-energy tensor must a static asymptotically flat spacetime metric be spherically symmetric, especially in the perfect-fluid case known as the static star conjecture?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a smooth four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ that is static and asymptotically flat: there exists a smooth, complete, hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector field $\xi$ on $M$, and outside a compact set the spatial slice (the quotient by the $\xi$-flow) is diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with the metric and lapse function approaching the standard flat values at the appropriate decay rates. Suppose the Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g = 8\pi T$ hold on $M$ for a stress-energy tensor $T$ supported in a compact "matter region" $\Omega \subset M$.

(a) Identify general structural conditions on the stress-energy tensor $T$ (for example, energy conditions, isotropy, equation-of-state hypotheses) which force the metric $g$ to be spherically symmetric, i.e. to admit an effective $SO(3)$ action by isometries whose orbits are the level sets of a radial function.

(b) (Static star conjecture.) In the special case where $T$ is the stress-energy tensor of a perfect fluid,
$$T_{\alpha\beta} = (\rho + p)\, u_\alpha u_\beta + p\, g_{\alpha\beta},$$
with $u$ the unit timelike four-velocity aligned with $\xi/\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$ inside $\Omega$, energy density $\rho \geq 0$, pressure $p \geq 0$ vanishing on $\partial\Omega$, and a barotropic equation of state $p = p(\rho)$ satisfying physically reasonable monotonicity conditions, prove that $(M,g)$ must be spherically symmetric, with $\Omega$ a metric ball.
artifact.category_tag: Static star rigidity in general relativity
artifact.status_search_result: The static star (fluid ball) conjecture remains open in full generality. Partial results are known: spherical symmetry has been established under additional hypotheses such as the existence of a spherically symmetric comparison model with the same equation of state and surface potential (Beig–Simon, Lindblom–Masood-ul-Alam), and recent work (Coutinho–Leandro and others) has further refined these conditions, but a fully general rigorous proof for arbitrary physically reasonable equations of state has not been obtained.

status_evidence.title: Static spherical perfect fluid stars with finite radius in general relativity: a review
status_evidence.snippet: Although it is considered physically evident, a rigorous proof that a static stellar model is spherically symmetric is still lacking.
status_evidence.claim: The full conjecture remains open as of this review.

status_evidence.title: On the uniqueness of static perfect-fluid solutions in general relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Uniqueness, in particular spherical symmetry, of a wide class of general relativistic, static perfect-fluid models is established provided there exists a spherically symmetric model with the same equation of state and surface potential.
status_evidence.claim: Conditional results yielding spherical symmetry are known.

status_evidence.title: On the fluid ball conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Work on the fluid ball conjecture concerning spherical symmetry of static perfect fluid spacetimes.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture continues to be actively studied.
